adjudication_changelog.quote: Persons 50 to 90 years of age were eligible for inclusion in the trials if they had mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer’s disease or had mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease (conditions previously referred to as prodromal Alzheimer’s disease and mild Alzheimer’s disease, respectively), in accordance with National Institute on Aging−Alzheimer’s Association diagnostic criteria. , Specifically, participants needed to have a CDR−Global Score (CDR-GS) of 0.5 or 1, indicating very mild or mild dementia, respectively.

title.value: Two Phase 3 Trials of Gantenerumab in Early Alzheimer’s Disease
title.quote:
Two Phase 3 Trials of Gantenerumab in Early Alzheimer’s Disease
**Authors:** R.J. Bateman, J. Smith, M.C. Donohue, P. Delmar, R. Abbas, S. Salloway, J. Wojtowicz
title.location: Title line and author line at the head of the document

design.value: Two phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials (GRADUATE I and GRADUATE II)
design.quote: The GRADUATE I and II trials were phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials. Participants were recruited from 288 sites in 30 countries

phase.quote: We conducted two phase 3 trials (GRADUATE I and II) involving participants 50 to 90 years of age with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease

n.quote: Of the 9993 persons who underwent screening, 1965 were enrolled in the trials; 985 were enrolled in the GRADUATE I trial and 980 in the GRADUATE II trial

n_description.value: Enrolled across the two trials (985 in GRADUATE I and 980 in GRADUATE II); in GRADUATE I 499 gantenerumab and 485 placebo, and in GRADUATE II 498 gantenerumab and 477 placebo, were randomly assigned and received at least one dose
n_description.quote: In the GRADUATE I trial, 499 and 485 participants were randomly assigned to receive gantenerumab and placebo, respectively, and received at least one dose of the trial drug or placebo.

population.value: Persons 50 to 90 years of age with mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer’s disease or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease (CDR-GS of 0.5 or 1, MMSE ≥22, FCSRT cueing index ≤0.67 and free recall ≤27) with evidence of amyloid plaques on PET or CSF testing
population.quote: participants 50 to 90 years of age with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease and evidence of amyloid plaques on positron-emission tomography (PET) or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing

followup.value: 116-week double-blind treatment period (initially planned as 104 weeks), with long-term safety follow-up visits 14 and 50 weeks after the last dose
followup.quote: The double-blind treatment period was initially planned to be 104 weeks and was extended to 116 weeks in response to delayed and missed visits due to the coronavirus disease 2019 (Covid-19) pandemic.

intervention.value: Subcutaneous gantenerumab escalated over 36 weeks to a target dose of 510 mg every 2 weeks, regardless of APOE ε4 genotype (120 mg every 4 weeks for three doses, then 255 mg every 4 weeks for three doses, then 510 mg every 4 weeks for three doses, then 510 mg every 2 weeks)
intervention.quote: During the double-blind treatment period, the gantenerumab dose was increased over a period of 36 weeks to a target level of 510 mg every 2 weeks, regardless of APOE ε 4 genotype.

comparator.value: Placebo, administered every 2 weeks in a 1:1 ratio
comparator.quote: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive gantenerumab or placebo, administered at a trial site or at home by a nurse.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The document reports specific measures to protect blinding (CDR raters unaware of group assignment and shielded from ARIA data, separate dosing personnel, blinded neuroradiologists) and reports sensitivity analyses concluding the primary findings did not result from unblinding of safety data.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The power calculation assumed approximately 1016 participants per trial group across both trials combined, while 1965 participants total were enrolled; the document also states pandemic-related missed visits would reduce power from 90% to 80%.
risk_of_bias.quote: We calculated that a sample of approximately 1016 participants per trial group (in both trials combined) would provide the trials with 90% power to detect a change from baseline in the CDR-SB score

disagreements.question: Does gantenerumab slow clinical decline in early Alzheimer's disease?
disagreements.position: It does not. Gantenerumab lowered amyloid plaque burden relative to placebo at 116 weeks but was not associated with slower clinical decline, and secondary clinical outcomes were not supportive of a beneficial clinical effect.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bateman et al., the GRADUATE I and II authors (this document)
disagreements.quote: Among persons with early Alzheimer’s disease, the use of gantenerumab led to a lower amyloid plaque burden than placebo at 116 weeks but was not associated with slower clinical decline.

disagreements.question: Did gantenerumab remove as much amyloid plaque as prior trials and modeling predicted?
disagreements.position: No. The magnitude of amyloid plaque removal was smaller than expected on the basis of previous trials and prespecified modeling predictions, and mean amyloid level on PET remained elevated after treatment.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bateman et al., the GRADUATE I and II authors (this document)
disagreements.quote: However, the magnitude of amyloid plaque removal was smaller than expected on the basis of previous trials and prespecified modeling predictions.

disagreements.question: Is rapid, near-complete plaque reduction required for anti-amyloid antibodies to show clinical efficacy?
disagreements.position: The document advances this as a hypothesis generated by these results taken with other anti-Aβ antibody trials, while explicitly stating the current trials did not test it.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bateman et al., the GRADUATE I and II authors (this document)
disagreements.quote: rapid plaque reduction, probably to a level below the threshold of detection, may be necessary to show clinical efficacy within the time frame of 18 to 27 months. However, the current trials did not assess this hypothesis.

disagreements.question: Do the greater brain-volume decreases and ventricular increases seen with gantenerumab indicate neurodegeneration?
disagreements.position: They may not reflect neurodegeneration, because amyloid plaque removal and fluid shifts could affect brain volume; the findings are similar to those in other amyloid-targeting trials.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bateman et al., the GRADUATE I and II authors (this document)
disagreements.quote: may not reflect neurodegeneration, given that amyloid plaque removal and fluid shifts could affect brain volume

disagreements.question: Are ARIA-E and amyloid plaque removal driven by the same mechanism?
disagreements.position: Probably not; observed ARIA-E incidence matched the predicted 25% while plaque removal was lower than predicted, which the authors say suggests different mechanisms drive ARIA-E and plaque removal.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bateman et al., the GRADUATE I and II authors (this document)
disagreements.quote: was in line with the prediction of 25% but amyloid plaque removal was lower than predicted suggests that different mechanisms may be involved in driving ARIA-E and plaque removal

disagreements.question: Is there a treatment effect on brain tau accumulation?
disagreements.position: No. There was no appreciable between-group difference in tau on PET in any of the four composite regions, despite lower CSF and plasma phosphorylated tau 181 with gantenerumab; the authors suggest the absence may be due to limited amyloid plaque removal.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bateman et al., the GRADUATE I and II authors (this document)
disagreements.quote: However, there was no treatment effect with respect to the accumulation of tau in the brain on PET; the absence of such an effect may be due to the limited amyloid plaque removal observed.
